summary: The video and bus logic is built as board hardware: the motion-object sequencer is a PAL written out as registered sum-of-products terms that steps through the H-phase slots, the VRAM is time-sliced by PVAS/VAS slot selects, the playfield uses a delay RAM for fine scroll, the line buffers are ping-pong buffers with write pointers loaded on /LD01, and DTACK comes from a 74LS163-style wait-state counter. Nothing follows MAME's screen_update / render_object / scanline_update split. The MAME influence shows up only at the edges: two PROMs that were never dumped are rebuilt to reproduce atarimo's tile-ordering and no-clip behaviour, the alpha colour bit order defaults to MAME's, and there are optional MAME-compat switches that are off by default.

findings.note: The MO list walk is a PAL16R6-style block. PVAS0/PVAS1 are combinational terms, and MC0/MC1/NEWMO/LD01 are registered SOP terms of 1H/2H/4H, MATCH, MATCHD and NXL, clocked every pixel. MAME instead walks the linked list once per band in a C loop.

findings.signal: VRAM slot multiplexing from raster bits
findings.note: One VRAM is shared between PF, MO link/word, alpha and CPU slots through 4:1 address muxes selected by registered VAS bits. A CPU access only happens when PVAS0&PVAS1 grant a slot (pvcpu), and the link register is strobed by /LINK.

DTACK is the RCO of a 4-bit counter. It is parallel-loaded from {VPA, CIN, BIN, /EEPROM}, enabled by a latched SD term and cleared by /AS, so wait states are produced the way discrete logic produces them. MAME models no such wait states.

findings.signal: Control words decoded at scan time
findings.note: The PFB/PFHSLD/MOHS/PFSPC/VIRQ/PFVS strobes come from a 3-to-8 decode of the alpha word as it is fetched during HBLANK on v[2:0]==7. PFVS loads a 9-bit PF vertical counter that increments on PFHST. MAME instead loops x=42..63 per scanline and applies a scroll-offset correction ('data - offset').

findings.signal: Playfield fine scroll via delay RAM
findings.note: Coarse scroll is a 6-bit tile counter preloaded from hscroll[8:3] at PFHST. Fine scroll is an 8-entry circulating delay RAM whose pointer is loaded with hscroll[2:0], and PF/M is selected per pixel from the PFSPC register. That is a pixel pipeline, not a tilemap with scrollx.

findings.signal: Priority/shade as PAL + GPC gate logic
findings.note: SHADE, PFWIN and M7 are sum-of-products over active-low line-buffer bits and PFX. CRAS1/CRAS0 come from NOR/NAND gate terms, then a registered colour-address mux and a STAIN flip-flop with preset/clear, all evaluated per pixel. MAME's two-pass bitmap merge with apply_stain is not reproduced.

findings.signal: Ping-pong line buffers with HPOS-loaded pointers
findings.note: Two buffer pairs (D and E RAMs) swap on RB0/RB1. Write pointers load HPOS on /LD01 and count, read pointers clear on /BUFCLR and erase behind the read, and the write enables are pen/priority SOP terms (including the pen-1 shade/stain encoding).

findings.signal: Hardware intensity arithmetic diverging from MAME
findings.note: The default path computes INT + {MOG,1} + 1 as a 4-bit adder (LS283) and keeps the hardware result. The MAME arithmetic (ztable index + 2*c) exists only behind DAC_MAME_COMPAT, which defaults to 0.

findings.signal: Undumped PROM contents reconstructed from atarimo semantics
findings.note: The 11N preset is computed as tile_row*(HSIZ+1), plus W-1 when flipped, and the 9J visibility bit is tied to 1 (no clipping). These reproduce MAME's row-major 'code++' tile order and its wrap-without-clip behaviour, rather than coming from the board.

findings.signal: Alpha colour bit order chosen to match MAME
findings.note: ALPHA_D_MAME defaults to 1 and reorders the GPC attribute pins to {VRD15,VRD12,VRD11,VRD10}, reproducing MAME's ((data>>10)&0x0f)|((data>>9)&0x20) instead of the alternate (literal) pin order.

The default SCOM path shifts the byte serially, one bit per /B4H, with start/stop framing. MAME's zero-latency mailbox is selectable via MAME_MAILBOX=0/1 but is off by default. These switches are comparison aids, not the organizing structure.
The decodes are written as LS138/LS139 select equations on address bits. Their 0x01F9 mirror masks necessarily match MAME's address map.
